assign.outcome:
**Doc check on landing, and no landing without an outcome — both wired and proved.** `Server/doc-check.mjs` (new) walks every module a landed task touched — the nearest directory at or above a touched file that has its own `page.js`, skipping the task's own `ai/**` notebook — and checks it has a `readme.md`, a `doc/` dir, and readme links that resolve. `Server/on-landing.mjs` now calls it and appends one log line; when something's missing it also posts one nag line on the task's card through Servex's `card_reply` (skipped when the task has no card). `.claude/hooks/ledger.mjs`'s `stop` branch now refuses a `landed_at` with no `outcome`: it blocks every time and logs the refusal once, before anything downstream (a future on-landing spawn included) would ever treat it as landed.

Proved in a scratch `LEDGER_ROOT`: a `landed_at` with no outcome blocks and logs the refusal exactly once even across repeated stops; adding an outcome clears the block with no new log line. Proved doc-check itself on a throwaway probe module (missing `doc/`, two dead links) both standalone and through `on-landing.mjs`, which also sent the real `card_reply` to a private Servex on :8195 (the probe module and probe task dir were deleted after). Also ran doc-check read-only against a real landed task from the main tree (`ai/2026-09-25/now-card-tabs`) — it correctly flagged `public/framework/ai2`'s readme for 3 dead links, two of which are a caveat rather than a bug: the check does a plain file/dir existence test, so a module whose `page.js` routes some readme links to *virtual* children (declared in code, no matching directory) can read as dead even though the site serves them fine — documented as a limitation in `Server/README.md` rather than built around, to keep the check this simple.

Brought forward as-is from other uncommitted work already sitting in the main tree, since this worktree had neither: `Server/on-landing.mjs` and its `Server/text-check.mjs` dependency (89 and 56 lines) — needed for the fenced file to exist at all before my own doc-check integration could attach to it.

Left alone: the spawn-on-landing wiring itself (calling `on-landing.mjs` from the ledger's `stop` branch) is not part of this brief's fence and isn't added here — the outcome refusal returns before that point regardless of whether or when that wiring lands.
